Liberation war secretary faces contempt charges
2017-10-18T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/city/liberation-war-secretary-faces-contempt-charges-1478014

The High Court yesterday issued a contempt of court rule against five government high officials, including the liberation war affairs secretary, for not complying with its directive over paying the monthly allowances to 13 freedom fighters.

The four others are director general of Jatiya Muktijoddha Council and its director (administration and finance), deputy secretary (law) and deputy secretary (budget) of liberation war affairs ministry.

The bench of Justice Quazi Reza-Ul Hoque and Justice Mohammad Ullah issued the rule following a contempt of court petition filed by the 13 freedom fighters from Rajshahi, Chapai Nawabganj and Naogaon as their monthly allowances had gone unpaid.

Petitioners' counsel Eunus Ali Akond told reporters that following a writ petition filed by his clients, the HC on March 21 this year directed the authorities concerned of the government to pay their monthly allowances regularly.

As the authorities did not take any step to comply with the HC directive, the freedom fighters on October 4 filed the contempt of court petition, he added.
